newsitem.title: NEPAL: American climbs Mount Everest for third time.
newsitem.headline: American climbs Mount Everest for third time.

text.p: An American mountain guide has scaled Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, for the third time, Nepal's Tourism Ministry said on Wednesday.
The ministry said Wallace Berg, a 42-year-old climber from Copper Mountain, Colorado, reached the 8,848-metre (29,028-foot) summit on Sunday with six Nepali sherpas.
Berg was the fourth American to climb Everest three times.
A total of 46 people have climbed Everest from the southern side this spring.

They include Australia's Tashi Tenzing, grandson of climber Tenzing Norgay who made the peak's first ascent with Edmund Hillary in 1953, the first Australian woman and the first three Icelanders to scale the summit.
The Tourism Ministry also said a team of four Italians and a Frenchman had reached the summit of the world's fourth highest mountain, Mount Lhotse, over the past three days.
France's Jean Christophe Lafaille scaled Lhotse, which stands next to Everest at 8,516 metres (27,940 feet), with Mario and Salvatore Panzeri on Wednesday.
Lafaille, from Gap, France, and Mario Panzeri, from Mandello del Lario in Lecco, are both 32-year-old mountain guides. Mario's brother, Salvatore, is a house painter who lives in Ballabio, Lecco.
Italian Simone Moro, a 29-year-old mountain guide from Colere, Bergamo, climbed Lhotse on Monday. He was followed on Tuesday by Abele Blanc, a 42-year-old guide from Aynavilles, Aosta.
Moro was the second Italian to scale Lhotse, and the first to climb it twice. Three Frenchmen have reached Lhotse's summit before Lafaille.
